newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia submits proposal on benchmark yield curve.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia submits proposal on benchmark yield curve.

text.p: Malaysia's Securities Commission said on Tuesday it has submitted to the government a proposal to build a benchmark yield curve in its effort to develop the ringgit bond market.
"This proposal to build a benchmark yield curve has already been submitted by the commission to the Minister of Finance for his consideration," said commission chairman Mohd Munir Majid.

"The successful implementation of this proposal would, we hope in time, remove one of the hurdles in the development of the ringgit bond market...the absence of a credible liquid benchmark," Munir told a bond market conference.
He said the supply-demand imbalance of Malaysian Government Securities has prevented a liquid benchmark yield curve which is default-risk free, from developing in the local bond market.

"It has been noted that without such a benchmark, the pricing of bonds in both the primary and secondary markets will be difficult and complicated; creating a situation which is not conducive to the growth of the local bond market," he said.
